current.text: He has a patella subluxation in his knee. He is officially out at least two weeks.
He should miss a couple of weeks and might miss week one. One expert guesses three to four weeks.
He is the backup center behind Domantas Sabonis and is on the projected bench.
With Raynaud and Dylan Cardwell both injured, Precious Achiuwa and a two-way big get the backup center minutes. The Kings may also play small with Ben Simmons at center.
As a backup he projects for about 19 to 20 minutes a night, and experts say he cannot do much in limited minutes.
His late-season jump last season came from many Kings injuries that opened a starting role. Over a full season of 56 starts at 30 minutes he ranked 156th in category leagues.
His upside depends on a Sabonis trade or injury. The Kings may try to move Sabonis's contract, but Josh does not expect a trade, and the team needs Sabonis to stay out of the relegation zone.
current.until: until Sabonis is traded or hurt

current.text: Do not draft him in a standard 12-team league. He is a backup and is injured. Josh adds he is not even the best per-minute producer among the backup options.
Ham thinks he could be better than Sabonis in two to three years and says the Kings should try to show he is a starter this season.
In Summer League he took 39% of his shots from three. If that three-point rate holds, his FG% would drop but his points and threes would rise. Keep an eye on it.
Experts expect the Kings to be one of the worst teams in the NBA, with poor coaching, ownership and front office, so their rotations are hard to predict.

durable.text: He shoots efficiently for a big man and helps in both FG% and FT%. He also makes some threes.
He blocks very few shots for a center.
His steals are far below the league pool.

note: Do not bid on him in our auction. He is a backup center behind Sabonis and has a knee injury. Yahoo ranks him 169th at an average cost of 1.0 USD and ESPN prices him at 0 USD, both outside our 144 drafted players. Watch the waiver wire for a Sabonis trade or injury. When he returns, check whether he keeps taking threes, which would trade some FG% for points and threes. He gives no blocks or steals, so he only adds FG%, FT% and low turnovers if he gets a starter's minutes.
